claim: Oura's spec describes API V2 as the only available integration point for Oura data and says the V1 API has been sunset.
quote: This document describes the Oura API Version 2 (V2), which is the only available integration point for Oura data. The previous V1 API has been sunset.

claim: Oura's getting-started page dates the V1 removal to January 22, 2024.
quote: The V1 API was removed on January 22nd, 2024.

claim: Personal access tokens were deprecated in December 2025 and are no longer available for use.
quote: personal access tokens were deprecated in December 2025 and are no longer available for use.

claim: API applications are limited to 10 users before requiring approval from Oura.
quote: By default, API Applications have a ten user limit. If you want to release your application to a wider audience, your application needs to be approved.

claim: There is no user limit once Oura approves the app.
quote: There is no limit once an application is approved.

claim: You submit the app for review from its page in the developer portal.
quote: Once you have finished developing your application, you can submit it for review from the application's page.

claim: Oura says users must consent to share each data type your app has access to.
quote: Oura users **must provide consent** to share each data type an API Application has access to.

claim: The API returns 403 when a request needs more permissions or the user's Oura subscription has expired.
quote: The requested resource requires additional permissions or the user's Oura subscription has expired.

claim: Oura's FAQ says a 403 usually means an expired subscription or a missing permission for the data type.
quote: This usually means the user's Oura subscription has expired or they haven't granted permission for the specific data type you're requesting.

claim: You create the Oura account in the Oura iOS or Android app and use it to sign in at cloud.ouraring.com.
quote: create an Oura account using the Oura iOS or Android application. Use the same account to sign-in to

claim: A registered application gets a client ID and client secret, and Oura says the secret should not be shared.
quote: A registered OAuth application is assigned a unique Client ID and Client Secret. The Client Secret should not be shared.

claim: Redirect URIs act as a whitelist the redirect_uri parameter must match exactly.
quote: The redirect URIs listed for your application act as a whitelist of allowed values, meaning this parameter must match one of the URIs exactly.

claim: The authorization URL is https://cloud.ouraring.com/oauth/authorize.
quote: Authorize: https://cloud.ouraring.com/oauth/authorize

claim: The token URL is https://api.ouraring.com/oauth/token.
quote: Access Token URL: https://api.ouraring.com/oauth/token

claim: Oura offers https://developer.ouraring.com/authorize as an alternative authorization URL for new OAuth clients.
quote: An alternative authorization URL is now provided at https://developer.ouraring.com/authorize for new OAuth clients.

claim: Oura labels the universal-link authorization URL as new.
quote: New: Universal Link Authorization URL

claim: On mobile devices with the Oura app installed the universal link can open the consent page inside the app.
quote: On supported mobile devices with the Oura app installed, this link can open the OAuth consent page within the app, where the user may already be logged in.

claim: Oura's authentication page lists eight scopes.
quote: You can request access to 8 different scopes of user data:

claim: The heartrate scope covers time series heart rate for Gen 3 users.
quote: heartrate Time series heart rate for Gen 3 users

claim: The spo2 scope covers the daily SpO2 average recorded during sleep.
quote: spo2 Daily SpO2 Average recorded during sleep

claim: The personal scope covers gender, age, height and weight.
quote: personal Personal information (gender, age, height, weight)

claim: The user can enable and disable scopes at consent.
quote: When an Oura user authorizes access to your application, she can enable and disable scopes based on her preferences.

claim: The spec's own scope list adds a ninth scope, heart_health (Heart health data).
quote: "spo2": "SpO2 Average recorded during sleep", "heart_health": "Heart health data"

claim: The scope parameter is space-separated and leaving it blank requests every scope.
quote: If left blank, the application will request all available scopes.

claim: Oura marks PKCE as recommended.
quote: code_challenge Recommended PKCE code challenge.

claim: The code_verifier is 43 to 128 characters, hashed with SHA-256 and base64url-encoded as code_challenge.
quote: between 43 and 128 characters long (inclusive), then hash it with SHA256 and encode the digest in base64url format without padding

claim: code_challenge_method must be S256.
quote: Value must be S256

claim: A refusal returns error=access_denied.
quote: If the user denies the request for authorization, the redirect will be to the same redirect URI, but with the parameter error=access_denied instead of the code parameter.

claim: The scope parameter on the redirect is deprecated and may be omitted.
quote: The scope query parameter is deprecated and may be omitted from the redirect; applications should not rely on it.

claim: Client credentials can go in the form body or as HTTP Basic.
quote: Instead of providing client_id and client_secret as parameters, they can be given using the HTTP Basic Authorization, with client_id as username and client_secret as password.

claim: The code exchange sends the code_verifier when a code_challenge was used.
quote: The original random string used to create the code_challenge in the authorization request.

claim: Oura's refresh token is single-use and invalidated after being used.
quote: The refresh token is single-use, meaning it is invalidated after being used.

claim: One troubleshooting section of the spec says access tokens typically expire after 24 hours.
quote: OAuth2 access tokens expire after a period (typically 24 hours for Oura).

claim: The spec's FAQ says tokens typically last 30 days.
quote: The token hasn't expired (they typically last 30 days)

claim: A reused refresh token comes back as already used or revoked.
quote: Token already used or revoked. If you are trying to use a refresh token, note that it can only be used once.

claim: The client-side flow has no refresh token and its token currently expires after 30 days.
quote: Note that the client-side only flow does not support refresh tokens. Once a token expires (currently set to 30 days), the user will need to re-authenticate your app.

claim: To revoke a token, call https://api.ouraring.com/oauth/revoke with the access token.
quote: https://api.ouraring.com/oauth/revoke?access_token={access_token}

claim: All data lives under https://api.ouraring.com/v2/usercollection/.
quote: curl -X GET https://api.ouraring.com/v2/usercollection/personal_info

claim: daily_activity holds daily activity summaries and activity levels.
quote: The Daily Activity scope includes daily activity summary values and detailed activity levels.

claim: daily_spo2 data is only available for users with a Gen 3 ring.
quote: The Daily SpO2 (blood oxygenation) routes include daily SpO2 average. Data will only be available for users with a Gen 3 Oura Ring

claim: daily_stress holds minutes in high stress and high recovery each day.
quote: The daily stress route includes a summary of the number of minutes the user spends in high stress and high recovery each day.

claim: daily_resilience is an estimate of resilience.
quote: Resilience is an estimate of your ability to withstand physiological stress and recover from it over time.

claim: daily_cardiovascular_age is a cardiovascular age estimate.
quote: Cardiovascular Age is an estimate of the health of your cardiovascular system in relation to your actual age.

claim: vO2_max holds VO2 max.
quote: VO2 Max is a measure of the maximum volume of oxygen that an individual can use during intense exercise.

claim: A user can have several sleep periods per day.
quote: A user can have multiple sleep periods per day.

claim: sleep_time is a recommended bedtime window calculated from sleep data.
quote: Recommendations for the optimal bedtime window that is calculated based on sleep data.

claim: heartrate is time-series heart rate in 5-minute increments.
quote: Heart rate is provided at 5-minute increments.

claim: session covers guided and unguided sessions.
quote: The Sessions data scope provides information on how users engage with guided and unguided sessions in the Oura app

claim: tag is deprecated in favor of enhanced_tag.
quote: Tag is deprecated. We recommend transitioning to [Enhanced Tag](#tag/Enhanced-Tag-Routes).

claim: ring_configuration holds the ring model, size and color.
quote: The Ring Configuration scope includes information about the user's ring(s). This includes the model, size, color, etc.

claim: rest_mode_period holds rest mode periods.
quote: The Rest Mode scope includes information about rest mode periods.

claim: ring_battery_level holds battery level documents.
quote: "summary": "Multiple Ring Battery Level Documents"

claim: personal_info holds the user's profile.
quote: The Personal Info scope includes personal information (e.g. age, email, weight, and height) about the user.

claim: List responses wrap records in a data array with a next_token.
quote: "required": [ "data", "next_token" ], "title": "MultiDocumentResponseDict"

claim: next_token comes back as a string or null.
quote: "next_token": { "anyOf": [ { "type": "string" }, { "type": "null" } ], "title": "Next Token" }

claim: The spec has a sandbox endpoint for each data type, serving fake data that you can access without an Oura account.
quote: Fake user data that you can access without an Oura account. There is a corresponding sandbox endpoint to each available data type.

claim: Sandbox endpoints live under /v2/sandbox/usercollection/.
quote: "/v2/sandbox/usercollection/daily_activity"

claim: Sandbox calls share your rate limit with the real data endpoints.
quote: The rate limit for the sandbox endpoints is shared with your rate limit on other data endpoints.

claim: Sleep data requires users to open the Oura app, while daily activity and stress may sync in the background.
quote: sleep data requires users to open the Oura app, while daily activity and stress may sync in the background

claim: Oura calls webhooks the preferred way to consume Oura data.
quote: Webhooks are the preferred way to consume Oura data

claim: Oura says customers who implement webhooks properly have not hit rate limits.
quote: We have not had customers hit rate limits with webhooks properly implemented

claim: The recommended pattern is one request for historical data when a user first connects, then webhooks.
quote: Make a single request for historical data when a user first connects, then use webhooks for ongoing updates

claim: Create one subscription per combination of event_type and data_type.
quote: You need to create separate subscriptions for each combination of:

claim: event_type is create, update or delete.
quote: "enum": [ "create", "update", "delete" ], "title": "WebhookOperation"

claim: Subscriptions are created with POST /v2/webhook/subscription.
quote: Call the `POST /v2/webhook/subscription` endpoint to register your webhook:

claim: The subscription call uses your app's x-client-id and x-client-secret headers.
quote: Client ID for webhook subscription endpoints. Must be used together with x-client-secret header.

claim: The subscription body has callback_url, verification_token, event_type and data_type.
quote: "required": [ "callback_url", "verification_token", "event_type", "data_type" ], "title": "CreateWebhookSubscriptionRequest"

claim: The data types you can subscribe to are listed in the spec, ending daily_stress, daily_cardiovascular_age, daily_resilience and vo2_max.
quote: "daily_stress", "daily_cardiovascular_age", "daily_resilience", "vo2_max" ], "title": "ExtApiV2DataType", "description": "Data types that partners can subscribe to via ExtApiV2 webhooks."

claim: Oura verifies the endpoint with a GET carrying verification_token and challenge.
quote: const { verification_token, challenge } = req.query;

claim: Respond with the challenge to activate the subscription.
quote: If verification succeeds, your subscription is activated

claim: Each event body carries event_type, data_type, object_id and user_id.
quote: const { event_type, data_type, object_id, user_id } = req.body;

claim: Events come with an x-oura-signature header.
quote: x-oura-signature: HMAC_SIGNATURE

claim: Events come with an x-oura-timestamp header.
quote: x-oura-timestamp: 1234567890

claim: The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the client secret.
quote: const hmac = crypto.createHmac('sha256', clientSecret);

claim: The HMAC covers the timestamp plus the JSON body.
quote: hmac.update(timestamp + JSON.stringify(body));

claim: The digest is hex, upper-case.
quote: const calculatedSignature = hmac.digest('hex').toUpperCase();

claim: Respond with a 2xx in under 10 seconds.
quote: Respond quickly (under 10 seconds) with a 2xx status

claim: Fetch the record by object_id afterwards.
quote: Use the object_id to fetch the complete data via the API

claim: Oura retries 10 times for 4xx responses.
quote: For 4xx responses: 10 retries

claim: Oura retries 10 times for 5xx responses.
quote: For 5xx responses: 10 retries

claim: Oura retries 10 times for timeouts.
quote: For timeouts: 10 retries

claim: Oura retries for about an hour.
quote: Oura will retry webhook deliveries for about an hour if your server doesn't respond properly.

claim: A 410 response cancels the subscription.
quote: Or respond with a 410 status code to automatically cancel

claim: DELETE /v2/webhook/subscription/{id} cancels a subscription.
quote: Use the DELETE endpoint: `DELETE /v2/webhook/subscription/{id}`

claim: Every subscription carries an expiration_time.
quote: "data_type", "expiration_time" ], "title": "WebhookSubscriptionModel"

claim: Renew a subscription with PUT /v2/webhook/subscription/renew/{id}.
quote: "summary": "Renew Webhook Subscription", "operationId": "renew_webhook_subscription_v2_webhook_subscription_renew__id__put"

claim: Notifications arrive about 30 seconds after data syncs from the app.
quote: Webhook notifications arrive approximately 30 seconds after data syncs from the mobile app.

claim: For longer outages, run a reconciliation job.
quote: It's a good practice to implement a reconciliation process that can fetch data for periods when your webhook might have been unavailable.

claim: The spec describes rate limits at two layers.
quote: The API enforces rate limits at two layers to ensure fair access across all applications:

claim: One layer is a per-access-token limit.
quote: a per-access-token limit, which throttles single-token floods, and

claim: The other is a per-application limit across all of an app's user tokens.
quote: a per-application limit, which caps the aggregate traffic across all of an application's end-user tokens

claim: Either returns 429 and X-RateLimit-Tier names the layer that fired.
quote: The `X-RateLimit-Tier` response header identifies which layer fired.

claim: Oura says to prefer the rate-limit headers over fixed-interval backoff.
quote: five headers are included to guide retries. Prefer these over fixed-interval backoff:

claim: The FAQ in the spec gives 5,000 requests per 5-minute period.
quote: The Oura API is limited to 5000 requests per 5-minute period.

claim: Oura's error-handling page gives 5,000 requests per 5-minute period.
quote: The API V1 and V2 API are rate limited to 5000 requests in a 5 minute period.

claim: Oura's FAQ suggests fetching history in date ranges of about one to three months.
quote: Use date range queries with reasonable time spans (e.g., 1-3 months at a time)

claim: Paging uses next_token.
quote: Implement pagination using the next_token parameter for large result sets

claim: Contact Oura if you expect to need higher limits.
quote: if you expect your usage to require higher limits.

claim: A missing-scope error lists the scopes the token needs.
quote: Missing required scopes. Your token must have the scopes listed as part of the detail of the error.

claim: Date parameters are interpreted in the user's local time zone.
quote: When querying data with date parameters, the dates are interpreted in the user's local timezone.

claim: Timestamps come back in ISO 8601 with time zone information.
quote: All timestamps in the Oura API use ISO 8601 format with timezone information.
